title: Fewer subscriptions
lede: What your card charges every month, what to do with each charge, and open-source tools that do the same thing for free. Example with made-up data.

subscriptions.name: Google Workspace
subscriptions.why: Email, Drive and Meet: it stays. But it went from $142.58 to $154.84 in August, which usually means one more user. Check for accounts nobody uses.

subscriptions.name: Anthropic (Claude)
subscriptions.why: Two plans: Max ($100) and Pro ($20). It's the tool that takes the most work off your plate.

subscriptions.name: Slack
subscriptions.why: Billed per active member, so the amount moves on its own.

subscriptions.name: Tango
subscriptions.why: Step-by-step guides with screenshots. A free extension does the same. Export your guides before you cancel.

subscriptions.name: CapCut
subscriptions.why: Only used for captions, and those already run free on your computer.

subscriptions.name: ElevenLabs
subscriptions.why: You already transcribe locally with mlx-whisper and the key is unused.

subscriptions.name: Lovable
subscriptions.why: $90 in June and $75 in July in credit top-ups; nothing since. Make sure no plan is still active.

items.title: Tango to Mimik
items.detail: Export the guides, install the extension, cancel.

items.title: CapCut to WolfCut
items.detail: Try it for a week on a real video before cancelling.

findings: The grocery store shows up every month, but it isn't software: left out.
Zoom had a failed charge in August and a good one in September. One real charge isn't enough to confirm it's monthly.
No hidden annual renewals: only Namecheap ($24.16 in April, domains).
not_seen: This review only sees this card. Anything you pay with another one doesn't show up here.
